speakers.summary: Polite and composed throughout. Repeats the cover offer after an initial refusal, then apologizes and proceeds with the phone-only purchase without showing frustration.

speakers.speaker: B
speakers.summary: Mostly straightforward and cooperative, with brief irritation when the salesperson repeats an unwanted cover offer. Returns to calm, practical discussion after the apology; the irritation does not persist.

frustration_moments.evidence: The reminder 'maine bola na' explicitly signals irritation at having to repeat the refusal. Voice analysis also identifies a firm, irritated delivery. Acoustic measurements show quieter, slower speech rather than an escalation in volume or speed, supporting a restrained rather than intense reaction.

Confirmation of whether a charger and cover come in the box.
Only the phone, with the bill in Amit Sharma's name and payment by UPI.
Opening the box to check the screen and camera.

phone ke saath lenge to yahi cover do sau ninyanve mein de doonga sir. alag se lene par poori keemat lagegi.

excluded_candidates: ji, neela hai. yahi chhah gb ram aur ek sau athais gb storage wala hai. nikaldu? -> Confirms the requested phone's availability and specifications; no higher-tier product is proposed.
charger aata hai, sir, cover nahi aata; phone, charger aur cable hai andar. -> Answers the customer's question about box contents; it does not offer an additional purchase.
upsell.pushy_reason: After the customer clearly said, “nahi, cover nahi chahiye. abhi bas phone lena hai,” the salesperson offered the cover again at a discounted price. This prompted an irritated second refusal, although the salesperson then apologized and stopped.
upsell.summary: The salesperson made two upsell attempts: a ₹499 cover offer and, after rejection, a ₹299 offer conditional on buying it with the phone. Both were rejected; after the customer's irritated reminder that they wanted only the phone, the salesperson apologized and completed the phone-only transaction.
upsell.customer_feedback: The customer reiterated, “maine bola na sirf phone chahiye,” objecting to being offered the cover again after already declining it.
upsell.coaching_feedback: You greeted the customer politely, clearly explained the box contents, and recovered from the second refusal by apologizing and proceeding with the phone-only bill. The key improvement is to accept “cover nahi chahiye” the first time rather than countering with a discount, because the customer's objection was wanting only the phone—not the cover's price.

conversations.topic: Wired mouse purchase and repeated upselling

speakers.speaker: A (salesperson)
speakers.summary: Remains controlled and persistently sales-focused despite repeated refusals, then apologizes and completes the requested purchase. Segment 27 is attributed to the customer based on its wording and voice label, rather than the transcript's salesperson label.

speakers.speaker: B (customer)
speakers.summary: Starts neutral and ready to buy, then becomes increasingly frustrated as repeated upselling disregards the stated budget, product choice, and urgency. Frustration peaks with emphatic refusals and a threat to leave. The purchase is completed, but the customer remains irritated about the wasted time.

upsell.pushy_reason: After the customer rejected wireless and repeated the ₹500 budget, the salesperson continued with a mousepad, a keyboard-mouse combo, another wireless pitch and an extended warranty. The offers continued despite explicit refusals and mounting frustration, ending only after the customer threatened to leave.
upsell.summary: Five upsell attempts were made, and all were rejected. The salesperson eventually apologized and billed only the selected wired mouse for ₹449. Speaker-label errors reduce confidence: the mousepad offer is attributed to the salesperson from its wording despite customer labels, while “Arey, kitni baar boloon” is treated as the customer's refusal, consistent with the mood notes.
upsell.customer_feedback: The customer wanted only the selected wired mouse within ₹500, objected to repeated extras and wasted time, and warned, “ab bill bana do warna main ja raha hoon”

unanswered_questions.question: mouse aur bill de do.
unanswered_questions.note: The bill had already been presented, but the transcript ends without a salesperson reply or confirmation that the mouse was handed over.

upsell.coaching_feedback: You initially matched the basic wired-mouse request and eventually recovered with “sirf wired mouse total four forty nine” and “Koi extra charge nahi.” Once the customer said “budget bola na, paanchso,” the most useful change was to stop offering extras and immediately bill the selected mouse; the subsequent combo, wireless and warranty pitches prolonged the transaction until the customer threatened to leave.

conversations.topic: Budget wired mouse demonstration and purchase

speakers.speaker: A
speakers.summary: Calm, cooperative exchanges about size, testing, warranty, and payment, ending with upbeat thanks. No complaints or frustration. This label appears to mix buyer and seller turns.

speakers.speaker: B
speakers.summary: Polite and helpful while explaining the price and offering a display model. Words and voice show no frustration; despite the customer label, these turns appear to be the seller's.

speakers.speaker: C
speakers.summary: Politely acknowledges payment and hands over the mouse and bill. No frustration evident in these brief closing turns.

customer_requested: A basic wired USB mouse for a laptop, costing no more than ₹300.
Check the mouse’s size and test that it works.
Pack a new sealed mouse and provide a bill.
excluded_candidates: ye wala dhai sau ka hai, wired hai, u s bee mein laga kar seedhe chala sakte hain. -> Recommends the requested wired USB mouse within the buyer’s ₹300 budget.
ek baar haath mein le kar dekh lo, -> Suggests checking the main product’s fit, not buying an additional or upgraded item.
haan ji, ye display wala dekh lijiye, isi model ka hai. -> Provides a display sample in response to the buyer’s size concern.
Bilkul. Is laptop mein laga deta hoon. Aap click aur scroll karke dekh lijiye. -> Fulfills the buyer’s request to test the mouse.
Ek saal ki company warranty hai. -> Answers the buyer’s warranty question; no paid protection or extended warranty is offered.
upsell.pushy_reason: No extra product, upgrade, or paid service was proposed, and there was no refusal or frustration to push past.
upsell.summary: No upsell was attempted: the buyer requested a basic wired USB mouse within ₹300 and purchased a ₹250 model after checking its size, operation, and warranty. Speaker labels are inconsistent: B delivers seller explanations, while A contains both buyer and seller turns; this lowers attribution confidence.
upsell.coaching_feedback: You matched the ₹300 budget with a ₹250 mouse and let the buyer test clicking and scrolling before purchase, directly addressing their practical concerns. When explaining “Ek saal ki company warranty hai,” also briefly explain how to claim warranty service, beyond advising the buyer to keep the bill.
